A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QLCoder work. All 37 pages of v3 and 38 pages of v5, including Appendices A–D, support comparison. Text and visual inspection establish reliable correspondence despite appendix reflow.

before.justification: v3 reports original query-synthesis, baseline, ablation, and runtime results on Java CVEs in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results, including 94 successful syntheses among 176 CVEs in Table 1 and the ablation and agent comparisons in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B–D retain the same synthesis loop, execution feedback, LSP/MCP tools, retrieval database, AST inputs, validator, and query templates. No algorithmic or architectural change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 176-CVE Java evaluation and the same benchmark comparisons and application scenarios. New Tables 8–9 identify the existing studies' 20-CVE subsets; every listed CVE already appears in v3 Table 7.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains Gemini Flash/Pro, GPT-5 minimal/medium, gpt-oss-20b, and Sonnet 4 configurations. Static-analysis and ablation comparators also remain unchanged. Section 4.1 now names configurations already evaluated in v3 Section 4.5 and Table 5.

E3.justification: The stated iteration budgets, CodeQL version, evaluation metrics, hardware, and sample sizes are retained. The expanded model wording and newly identified CVE subsets do not establish changed experimental procedures or settings.

E4.justification: Table 4 revises the full-system ablation reference success rate from 55% to 50%, narrowing the reported component-removal gaps by five percentage points. The ablation variants, cutoff and scalability analyses, case studies, and Figure 7 error counts remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Numerical corrections do not disclose additional runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing result entries are revised. Table 4 changes QLCoder success from 55% to 50%. Table 5 changes Flash compilation without/with QLCoder from 19%/24% to 0%/45%, Pro without QLCoder from 35% to 60%, and GPT-5 minimal/medium with QLCoder from 24%/55% to 35%/80%. The corresponding gpt-oss-20b and Sonnet 4 rates change from 35% and 100% to 45% and 99%. Agent success rates and the main 94/176 success and 0.700 F1 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal synthesis requirements in Section 3.1 and metric definitions in Section 4.2 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises proofs, theorems, or mathematical assumptions.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows QLCoder's reported compilation rate from 100% to 99.4% and raises the quoted Gemini baseline rate from 19% to 60%, reducing the stated compilation advantage. The main contributions, 53.4% synthesis success claim, and F1 claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of component usefulness, scalability, applicability, and failure conditions are retained. Section 7 and Appendix A.1 preserve the same Java-only coverage, training-cutoff, agent-interface, and IRIS evaluation limitations.

D1.justification: New Appendix A Tables 8–9 disclose the CVE identifiers, CWE categories, and projects for the ablation and cross-model subsets. This improves experiment identification. Implementation details, hardware, prompts, tool specifications, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and comparisons with prior research. The acknowledgment changes do not alter scholarly positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: There are limited edits to the experimental-setup wording and acknowledgments, with the narrative and section order retained. Appendix A also changes several runtime references from Table 7 to Table 9 incorrectly; the runtime data remain in Table 7.

P2.justification: v5 adds two compact CVE-list tables and redraws Figure 7 with revised spacing and colors, including changing fixed-version false-positive flows from green to red. Its counts remain unchanged. Subsequent appendices reflow without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 improve reproducibility by identifying both experimental subsets, while several Table 5 compilation corrections now agree with Figure 7's retained error counts. Figure 7 also distinguishes false positives more clearly. These limited gains outweigh reporting regressions: erroneous runtime references to Table 9 and an unexplained 99% Claude compilation rate in a comparison labeled as covering 20 CVEs.
